outputs.exact_statement:
Let $K,M\subset\mathbb R^n$ be convex bodies, with the origin interior to $K$. Then $$\begin{aligned}
 \left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{0+}|K+tM|
 &=n\kappa_n\mathbb E_{\sigma}\!\left[g_K(u)^{-n}
                 h_M\bigl(\nabla g_K(u)\bigr)\right]
                 \label{eq:minkowski-volume-derivative}\\
 &\ge n|K|^{(n-1)/n}|M|^{1/n}.\nonumber
\end{aligned}$$ Equality in the inequality holds if and only if $K$ and $M$ are homothetic up to translation. The derivative identity remains valid when $M$ is an arbitrary nonempty compact convex set.

The spaces $\mathcal H_l$ form an orthogonal decomposition of $L^2(\sigma)$, and $\Delta_SY=-\lambda_lY$ for $Y\in\mathcal H_l$. Every even $H\in C^1(S^{n-1})$ satisfies $$\label{eq:spectral-gap}
 \lambda_2\mathop{\mathrm{Var}}(H)+(\lambda_4-\lambda_2)\left\lVert QH\right\rVert_2^2
 \le \mathbb E_{\sigma}\left|\nabla_SH\right|^2,
 \qquad \lambda_2=2n,\quad \lambda_4=4(n+2).$$

For even $C^1$ functions, $$\label{eq:sign-operator}
 \mathcal B(f_1,f_2)
 =\left\langle f_1,
   \left[C+\left(\frac{2p}{k}+\frac{p^2}{k^2}\right)(C-P)\right]
   f_2\right\rangle.$$

For every nonzero symmetric positive semidefinite $A$, there is a unique origin-symmetric convex body $L_A$ in $V=\mathop{\mathrm{range}}(A)$ that minimizes [eq:variational-objective] subject to $\tau_A(L_A)=1$. Denote its extended gauge by $g_A$.
The map $A\mapsto g_A|_{S^{n-1}}$ is continuous on $\mathcal A$ in the uniform norm.
Every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space has a fixed point.
There is a symmetric positive definite matrix $A$ with $\det A=1$ such that $g_A^k$ has zero component in $\mathcal H_2$.

Let $\eta,\zeta$ be finite positive measures on $\mathbb R^n$ with bounded, spanning support. Suppose that both satisfy [eq:functional-condition]. Then $$\label{eq:bilinear} \iint |x\cdot y|\,d\eta(x)d\zeta(y)\ge b_n.$$ If equality holds, there is an origin-centered ellipsoid $E_0$ such that $$\int h_{E_0}\,d\eta=(|E_0|/\kappa_n)^{1/n}.$$

Let $n\ge3$, let $B=-B\subset\mathbb R^n$ be the unit ball of a real normed space, and let $C\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a convex body. Write $B^\circ$ for the polar unit ball and put $I_B=\Pi(B^\circ)/\kappa_{n-1}$. Normalize the Holmes–Thompson volume and boundary area by $$\mathcal V_B(C)=\frac{|B^\circ|}{\kappa_n}|C|,
 \qquad
 \mathcal A_B(\partial C)=nV(C[n-1],I_B),$$ where $V(C[n-1],I_B)$ is mixed volume with $n-1$ copies of $C$, normalized by $V(C[n])=|C|$. Then $$\label{eq:holmes-thompson}
 \mathcal A_B(\partial C)^n
 \ge n^n\kappa_n\,\mathcal V_B(C)^{n-1}.$$ Equality holds if and only if $B$ is an ellipsoid and $C=x+tB$ for some $x\in\mathbb R^n$ and $t>0$.

hypotheses.statement: Let $T_{10}=\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_{10})\subset\mathbb R^{10}$, where the $e_i$ are the coordinate unit vectors, and let $K=T_{10}\times T_{10}\subset\mathbb R^{20}$.
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a full-dimensional convex polytope.
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^r$ and $B\subset\mathbb R^s$ be full-dimensional convex polytopes, where $r,s\ge2$.
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a convex body.

For $d\ge2$, the standard simplex $T_d=\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $$|T_d|=\frac1{d!},\qquad
 |\Pi T_d|=\frac{d+1}{((d-1)!)^d},\qquad
 R_d(T_d)=c_d.$$

There exist a constant $\lambda>1$ and an integer $N\ge20$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, some full-dimensional convex polytope $K_n\subset\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $$\frac{R_n(K_n)}{R_n(T_n)}\ge\lambda^n.$$

outputs.exact_statement: Let $P\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, be a convex body. For every invertible linear map $L\colon\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$, $$\Pi(LP)=|\det L|L^{-t}\Pi P,\qquad R_d(LP)=R_d(P),$$ where $L^{-t}$ denotes the inverse transpose. Translations also preserve $R_d$.

For $d\ge2$, the standard simplex $T_d=\mathop{\mathrm{conv}}(0,e_1,\ldots,e_d)\subset\mathbb R^d$ satisfies $$|T_d|=\frac1{d!},\qquad
 |\Pi T_d|=\frac{d+1}{((d-1)!)^d},\qquad
 R_d(T_d)=c_d.$$ Every full-dimensional $d$-simplex has the same value $c_d$.

There exist a constant $\lambda>1$ and an integer $N\ge20$ such that, for every integer $n\ge N$, some full-dimensional convex polytope $K_n\subset\mathbb R^n$ satisfies $$\frac{R_n(K_n)}{R_n(T_n)}\ge\lambda^n.$$ The polytopes $K_n$ may be chosen as Cartesian products of simplices.
